messages.subject: Re: My MapReduce does not return all values
parts:
It looks to me you are selecting only the first value with [[1]], somewhere near the middle of your code. Please remember the map function is vectorized, that is gets as arguments multiple records. This may be different from what you are used with python or earlier versions of rmr, but is essential for speed and not unusual  in R circles.

Antonio

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

require('rmr2');
require('rhdfs');
hdfs.init()
hdfs.rmr("/user/michael/rMean")

            output = output,
            input.format = 'text',

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#467] Re: My MapReduce does not return all values
parts:
This solution  is also better from a software engineering point of view as the parsing logic is isolated out of the map logic and you are also reusing existing code. The only thing is that print(fields) statement. We advise users that standard output in the mapper and reducer function is reserved for use by hadoop. In addition to that, rmr  captures user generated output to standard output and redirects it to standard error for the same functions. So if everything works as it should, those print statements output should be in the logs under stderr. If you plan to run this on a serious amount of data, writing all your data in the error logs is not  a good idea.


Antonio

This is an old thread but my "broken" example is based on code posted here. My R script is:
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

#
# Based on Breen's Example 2: airline
#

library(rmr2)

# assumes 'airline' and airline/data exists on HDFS under user's home directory

hdfs.data.root = 'airline'
hdfs.data = file.path(hdfs.data.root, 'data')

# unless otherwise specified, directories on HDFS should be relative to user's home
hdfs.out.root = hdfs.data.root
hdfs.out = file.path(hdfs.out.root, 'out')

mapper.year.market.enroute_time = function(k, fields) {
# Skip header line in csv formatted file
  if (!(as.character(fields[[1]]) == "Year")) {
    keyval(as.character(fields[[9]]), 1)
  }
}

reducer.year.market.enroute_time = function(key, vv) {
# count values for each key
  keyval(key, sum(as.numeric(vv),na.rm=TRUE))
}

mr.year.market.enroute_time = function (input, output) {

mapreduce(input = input,
            output = output,

input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
            map = mapper.year.market.enroute_time,
            reduce = reducer.year.market.enroute_time)
}

results.df = as.data.frame(out,stringsAsFactors=F )
colnames(results.df) = c('carrier', 'count')
print(results.df)

The problem is that I supply a csv file with a header as input data and I "lose" the first chunk of data in the results. If I process a small file, then the first half of the rows in the dataset are not processed.

Is there anything wrong with my map or reduce functions? I am using the provided csv input format. This is consistent whether I am hosted on a Cloudera VM or a Hortonworks VM.

I doubt this is a bug in rmr2 but want to see if I am doing something silly/wrong.

Jim

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#531] Re: My MapReduce does not return all values
parts:
Unfortunately you can only use header-less csv files. It's a limitation that has to deal with the way hadoop splits the data and I don't see a fix coming  in the short term. If you want you can add column names to the make.input.format call using the same syntax as for read.table, but you need to remove headers or at the very list you'll get character or factors where numeric data is expected. Exactly why you would lose the first chunk though is not clear, it seems like read.table fails on the first chunk and then that chunk is skipped silently. This is something I would like to fix. Could you open an issue on the rmr2 repo? Thanks


Antonio

On Sunday, December 30, 2012 12:22:32 AM UTC-5, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
This solution  is also better from a software engineering point of view as the parsing logic is isolated out of the map logic and you are also reusing existing code. The only thing is that print(fields) statement. We advise users that standard output in the mapper and reducer function is reserved for use by hadoop. In addition to that, rmr  captures user generated output to standard output and redirects it to standard error for the same functions. So if everything works as it should, those print statements output should be in the logs under stderr. If you plan to run this on a serious amount of data, writing all your data in the error logs is not  a good idea.


Antonio
